messages:

Can Redwood propose language and the economics that would minimize our downside while keeping you protected on minimum throughput?

—Lisa

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Clearpoint - request for 6mo opt-out + ramp schedule (Deal Desk approval request)

Marissa / Karthik,

Quick summary: Clearpoint (Strategic Health SaaS) is asking for an opt-out at month 6 with a pro-rated credit bucket and a staged ramp (they want to avoid paying top-tier committed units while adoption ramps). They’re otherwise signing for 18mo reserved capacity.

Proposed commercial approach I modeled:
- Month 1–3: 100% committed units (onboarding heavy)
- Month 4–6: 75% committed units (expected feature adoption)
- Opt-out window at month 6 with 30-day notice. If they opt out, offer a one-time credit equal to 30% of remaining committed fees (capped at $X) plus a 90-day gradual ramp-down where we reduce reserved capacity in two equal steps to their observed 30-day usage baseline.
- If they do not opt out, the remainder of term follows standard committed schedule.

Trade-offs we need to approve: discounting credit vs. locking in revenue and preserving offboarding operational cost recovery. I attached a spreadsheet showing net present value across three adoption curves.

Requests:
1) Deal Desk signoff on the credit cap and ramp cadence; I recommend we cap the credit at 30% of remaining committed fees and run the two-step ramp (50% reduction at day 30 post-opt, remaining 50% at day 90).
2) Exec approval for any deviation from standard early-termination language (legal will need the exact clause before we present to customer).

I’m standing by if you want to jump on a 20-min call.

Thanks,
Dylan
attachments: ramp-schedule-proposal.xlsx, Clearpoint_TermSheet_v3.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clearpoint - request for 6mo opt-out + ramp schedule (Deal Desk approval request)

Dylan — good framing and thanks for the spreadsheet. I reviewed the numbers quickly:

- I’m comfortable with a one-time credit bucket but we should tie the credit cap to a fixed dollar cap (not a percentage of remaining fees) to avoid blowouts in large deals. Recommend cap = $125k.
- I prefer the two-step ramp cadence you proposed (day 30 / day 90) but change first step to 40% / 60% — faster initial relief for the customer while preserving runway recovery for Redwood.
- Require a conditioning clause: Customer must provide 30 days notice and a short adoption report (key metric: active monthly inference calls) to be eligible for the credit. This prevents opportunistic opt-outs.

Karthik — if you agree, please escalate this to Markus for executive signoff on the cap and the changed cadence. We’ll have legal draft precise clause language once Markus okays the economics.

Marissa
VP, North America Sales Ops
attachments: none

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clearpoint - request for 6mo opt-out + ramp schedule (Deal Desk approval request)

Thanks team — reviewed the proposal. Executive position:

- Approve the one-time credit bucket with a hard cap of $125,000.
- Approve ramp cadence of 40% reduction at day 30, remainder 60% reduction at day 90 post-opt-out notice.
- Require the conditioning clause Marissa suggested: 30-day written notice + submission of adoption report tied to agreed metric (active monthly inference calls).
- Insert a make-whole recovery mechanism: if customer resumes equivalent production within 180 days, remaining credit can be reclaimed pro-rata.

Karthik/Legal — please produce the exact clause text for inclusion in TermSheet_v4 and route for signature. Dylan — you may present the proposed paragraph to the customer after legal drafts.

Markus
Chief Commercial Officer, Redwood Inference
attachments: none

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Cheng <lisa@clearpointhealth.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@clearpointhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Final: proposed opt-out & staged offboard language (Clearpoint)

Lisa / Tom — thank you for the candid ask and patience while we worked this through internally. Below is the commercial summary we can commit to subject to legal wording:

- Opt-out window: month 6 with 30-day written notice.
- One-time offboard credit: credit applied at opt-out equal to up to $125,000 (hard cap), paid as a credit against remaining committed fees.
- Staged ramp: after notice, Redwood will reduce Reserved Capacity by 40% at day 30 and by the remaining 60% at day 90, aligned to observed 30-day usage baseline reported by customer.
- Eligibility: customer must submit an adoption report (active monthly inference calls) covering the 30 days prior to notice to qualify for the credit.
- Make-whole clause: if customer resumes equivalent usage within 180 days, Redwood may reclaim unused portion of the credit pro-rata.

If this economic summary is acceptable I will have legal draft the exact paragraph into TermSheet_v4 and send a DocuSign for signatures. DocuSign preview link: https://docusign.net/clearpoint_deal_3419

Can you confirm by EOD Friday whether you want us to proceed to signature?

Best,
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
